method: Eighth clause checked this session, next in `npm run queue` after hb_accommodation. Different in kind from the seven before it: this clause's live content is not the static body text but five jurisdiction-specific factual claims pulled in by {{annualReportRule}} from templates/taxonomy.json (DE, CA, TX, FL, NY filing schedules for the annual report / Statement of Information / Public Information Report). These are administrative filing-deadline facts, not judicial doctrine, so the method used for the prior seven clauses (find the controlling opinion, read it) does not transfer cleanly. Tried it anyway rather than assuming it wouldn't work: three CourtListener searches, one per state with the most specific statutory/agency language available (CA Corporations Code section 1502, DE 8 Del. C. section 502, TX franchise-tax Public Information Report). None returned an opinion that states or corroborates the specific deadline. This is the expected result for this kind of claim -- courts cite these statutes in passing (standing, forfeiture, dissolution disputes) but do not restate filing deadlines as part of a holding the way Brinker restates the meal-break standard -- and reusing an incidental case mention just to produce a citation would be exactly the kind of thin corroboration this project's method exists to avoid. egress to every primary source that would actually confirm these five deadlines (www.sos.ca.gov, and the parallel DE/TX/FL/NY equivalents, none of which are even in the source registry) remains blocked; re-probed the same day via npm run probe, unchanged (0 of 21 registry hosts reachable).
queries: California Statement of Information biennial corporation deadline Corporations Code section 1502 (CourtListener)
Delaware annual report franchise tax March 1 8 Del. C. section 502 (CourtListener)
Texas franchise tax Public Information Report May 15 deadline forfeiture (CourtListener)

assertions.text: Delaware: annual report due March 1 for corporations; LLC annual tax due June 1
assertions.note: No opinion found in three CourtListener searches states or corroborates this deadline. Not a defect in the clause -- this is simply not the kind of fact litigated opinions restate -- but it means the claim is unverified by the only source this session's tooling can reach.

assertions.text: California: Statement of Information within 90 days of formation, then biennially (LLC) or annually (corporation)
assertions.note: Same result. leginfo.legislature.ca.gov (Corporations Code section 1502) and www.sos.ca.gov, the two sources that would actually confirm this, are both in the registry and both blocked (http-403, re-probed 2026-08-21).

assertions.text: Texas: Public Information Report with the franchise tax report, due May 15

notes: Florida and New York's annualReport entries were not separately searched after the DE/CA/TX pattern held for all three tried -- a fourth and fifth search were very unlikely to change the conclusion that CourtListener does not carry this kind of fact, and running them would have been process for its own sake rather than a real check.
No primary or agency host for any of the five states is currently reachable, so none of these five deadlines can be moved off unsourced this session by any method available.
This clause's registered-agent sentence ('a lapsed agent is the most common cause of a missed filing') is a practice claim, not a legal one, and was not part of this check.

gaps left empty deliberately: gaps in this project's scoring means 'a source described a requirement the clause omits,' and no source was reached to describe anything. The right label for zero corroborating sources is insufficient-sources, not incomplete -- an empty gaps array here is accurate, not an oversight.
toolLimitation: CourtListener (the one host reachable this session) indexes judicial opinions, not administrative filing schedules. It corroborated seven clauses' case-law claims this session but is structurally the wrong tool for a clause whose content is state-by-state statutory deadlines with no associated litigation. Recorded here rather than skipped silently, per this project's rule against fabricating a check that didn't happen.
